name: The Red Audit — Corporate Satire Mural Series
creator: Anonymous collective known as Ledger
description: A coordinated series of photorealistic murals appearing overnight on the exterior walls of corponation district offices across GLMZ, each depicting a specific corporate executive rendered in the style of classical Dutch accounting portraits — but surrounded by itemized lists of their company's documented human rights violations, rendered in meticulous calligraphy. The murals use a proprietary paint compound that resists standard chemical removal for up to ninety days. Over four years, forty-three murals appeared across Tiers 2 through 4.
cultural_impact: Forced several corponations into public-facing accountability responses for the first time in decades; the image of NovaMed director Sung-Bae Christiansen surrounded by worker casualty statistics became one of the most reproduced images in M88 underground media.
controversy: Three people were arrested under the Corponation Property Integrity Act in 2206 and later acquitted; Ledger's identity remains unknown and the collective is believed to have changed membership entirely at least twice.
story_hooks: A character is approached to join Ledger for the most dangerous mural yet — targeting the Spire's own residential facade.
Someone is selling what they claim is the Ledger formula for the removal-resistant paint, and a buyer wants to use it for something far less principled.
A former Ledger member has been disappeared, and the last mural they painted contains a hidden message only someone who knows the collective's internal codes can read.
